text:
maria-cs: FYI acme-platform is stuck onboarding, they hit auth failures during SDK init. Customer says it worked in sandbox but fails in prod. 

acme-platform: @maria-cs reproduction steps: msal-node auth flow, exchange refresh token -> get 401 from AAD on our backend. Happens after ~10m of idle. No 429s.

maria-cs: Can you paste the error body? :eyes:

acme-platform: logs (sanitized):
```
{
  "error":"invalid_grant",
  "error_description":"AADSTS50071: The request is not within the allowed time range.
Trace ID: 12345
Correlation ID: abcde
Timestamp: 2026-03-23 14:12:11Z"
}
```

dan-devexp: AADSTS50071 points to clock skew or token TTL/time-sync with their IDP. But they said only prod, sandbox OK. Could be conditional access re-eval in prod (device compliance) causing AAD to reject refresh.

jules-engr: Also check if their refresh token is being reused from a long-running worker. Azure refresh tokens can be invalidated by Conditional Access if the device session isn't MFA/compliant.

kevin-sre: Quick checks: 1) server NTP drift on their side, 2) are they using the same client_id/client_secret across envs, 3) are there CA policies scoped to production tenant/app.

acme-platform: We ran `ntpstat` on prod host — time is OK. App registration same credentials. They confirmed a conditional access policy that blocks non-compliant devices in prod.

maria-cs: That matches. Conditional Access will require fresh interactive auth in some cases, causing refresh_token to become invalid. For onboarding, that means their CI/workers can't complete automated init.

dan-devexp: Short-term workaround: configure the SDK to perform an initial interactive auth (or device code flow) during onboarding so CA evaluation happens with a compliant device, then persist a valid refresh token. Long-term: their IT can whitelist the app or exempt the specific service principal for the CA policy during onboarding window.

acme-platform: Is there anything on our side we should change? We get a 401 with AADSTS code and then our SDK retry loops just keep failing.

jules-engr: On Redwood side, we can: 1) change error message propagation to include AADSTS code so CS + customer can triage faster, 2) add a short onboarding doc section called "Azure AD Conditional Access — common gotchas" with recommended flows (device code/device auth, whitelisting, token lifetimes).

maria-cs: Action items: @dan-devexp add a clearer error sink for AADSTS codes (task), @jules-engr draft a 1-page CA onboarding note for docs, @acme-platform try device-code flow and report back in this thread.

kevin-sre: Also, recommend they avoid long-lived worker-run initializations that reuse tokens after long idle. If they must, rotate tokens using an interactive refresh path periodically.

acme-platform: Trying device code now — will update in ~15m. Thanks.

opsbot: ticket #CS-1992 created for acme-platform onboarding auth failure (linked to this thread).

acme-platform: Update — device-code flow worked, onboarding completed. Thanks for the pointer.

maria-cs: Great, closing loop. I'll add doc blurb and record renewal-risk as low but note initial friction for future signals. :white_check_mark:

dan-devexp: Follow-up: opened issue to surface AADSTS codes in SDK errors: https://redwood.internal/issue/1234

jules-engr: Drafted doc snippet and pushed to /docs/onboarding/azure-ad-conditional-access.md (internal) — will attach to the customer onboarding checklist.

maria-cs: Customer feedback captured: ask for an "Azure AD quickstart" in our onboarding flow so non-expert IT teams can avoid this. Logged in CS notes.

acme-platform: Thanks team, resolved for now. We'll recontact if our IT tightens CA policies.
